key_insight: METTA proposes memory-enhanced test-time adaptation to help reinforcement learning agents adapt to unfamiliar tasks using limited interaction. It targets the challenge of using evidence accumulated over long interaction histories.
problem_solved: Recurrent agents compress past experience into hidden states, potentially losing useful task evidence, while transformer-based agents retrieve past trajectories at quadratic memory and computation cost.
method: Use a meta-reinforcement learning framework to learn how to adapt quickly to unseen tasks.
Introduce memory-enhanced test-time adaptation to support the use of historical task evidence.

impact: METTA targets a practical bottleneck in adaptive agents: using long interaction histories without expensive trajectory retrieval. Efficiency gains and adaptation improvements cannot be verified from the provided excerpt.
